solutions.title: Business funding
solutions.headline: Keep your cash flow moving.
solutions.intro: A new contract. A growth opportunity. A facility coming to an end. Start with the purpose, then understand the borrowing that could fit your cash flow and plans.
solutions.goal: Manage cash flow or fund growth
uses: Bridge the timing between paying suppliers, holding stock and receiving customer payments.
Fund your next stage of growth
Frame the funding needed for a new contract, expansion or acquisition around a credible commercial plan.
Explore the purpose, timing and commitments behind refinancing, rather than comparing headline rates alone.
fit: An operating business with a clear purpose for the funds
A credible repayment case and a view of existing obligations
Decision-makers ready to discuss timing, cost and security
solutions.notFit: A recurring loss without a credible plan needs a different assessment from a temporary cash-flow gap. A pre-revenue company seeking risk capital may need an equity conversation.
solutions.mechanics: Business borrowing comes in different forms. A term facility, receivables-based funding and asset finance serve different needs. The useful starting point is how the funds will be used, how repayments could be made and which obligations the business can support.
tradeoffs: Total cost
Look beyond the headline rate. Understand interest, arrangement and intermediary fees, any exit charges and the assumptions behind a comparison.
Repayments and flexibility
Match payment dates and duration to cash generation. Clarify early repayment, renewals, increases and what happens if trading changes.
Security and guarantees
A provider may require business security or personal guarantees. Requirements vary; understand the specific exposure before committing.
Assessment and timing
A first response is different from approval or drawdown. Information, credit assessment, documentation and any security arrangements affect the timetable.
prepare: What the funding must achieve
Approximate amount, duration and any important deadline
How the business expects to repay and what it already owes
faqs: Can you help if my bank has declined?
The reason for the decision matters. A different provider or structure may consider a different case, but a decline does not establish that funding will be available elsewhere.
Will I need a personal guarantee?
That depends on the provider, structure and assessment. Any proposed guarantee and its implications need to be made clear before a commitment.
Will an enquiry affect my credit file?
An enquiry is not a credit application. The actual assessment process and any proposed credit searches should be explained before they happen.

solutions.valueHeading: Turn the trading plan into a funding case

solutions.valueIntro: We help organise the requirement, clarify the information needed and coordinate a relevant funding conversation. The scope of any preparation or advisory work is agreed separately.

solutions.title: Property finance
solutions.headline: Build the next project on firmer foundations.
solutions.intro: Acquisition, development or refinancing: the right conversation starts with the asset, the delivery programme and a realistic exit.
uses: Set out the asset, ownership structure, available equity and acquisition timetable.
Connect planning, build costs, contingency and staged cash requirements to a credible delivery plan.
Review a maturing facility, a completed scheme or capital tied up before sales or a longer-term refinance.
fit: An identifiable property or project and a defined funding purpose
A view of equity, delivery capability and relevant experience
A realistic repayment, sale or refinancing plan
solutions.notFit: A property idea without a worked-through project or exit needs preparation first. This business-capital journey should not be treated as personal residential mortgage advice.
solutions.mechanics: A property facility needs to fit the asset and its stage. Development funding may draw in stages against progress; an acquisition or refinance has different conditions. Valuation, equity, legal work and the proposed exit all influence the assessment.
tradeoffs: Usable funds and your contribution
Clarify the net funds available after costs, the equity contribution and which costs must be met before or alongside lender funds.
Drawdowns and conditions
Understand valuation, monitoring, legal and other conditions, including when money can actually be released.
Interest and fees
Consider the whole project cost, including arrangement, monitoring, legal and exit charges where applicable.
Term and exit
Test sales or refinance assumptions, contingency and what happens if delivery or sales take longer. An extension should not be assumed.
prepare: Property type, region and acquisition or project stage
Costs, equity, planning position and relevant experience
Required date, programme and proposed exit
faqs: Can funding complete by my deadline?
That depends on the asset, available information, valuation, legal work and the provider’s conditions. Share a real deadline early so the critical path can be considered.
How much equity will I need?
Requirements depend on the provider, asset and project. A single published lender limit is not a universal rule.
Can I refinance a completed development?
A development exit or other refinance may be a relevant conversation, subject to the property, existing borrowing, timing and a credible exit.

solutions.commitmentsHeading: Equity, drawdowns and the exit plan
solutions.valueHeading: Build the funding case around the programme
solutions.enquiryIntro: Start with property type, region and acquisition or project stage. Keep the first email non-confidential; we will agree any detailed information exchange before proceeding.
solutions.fitIntro: Use these discussion points to frame the requirement. Provider assessment determines suitability, availability and terms.
solutions.valueIntro: We help organise the requirement, clarify the information needed and coordinate a relevant funding conversation. The scope of any preparation or advisory work is agreed separately.

solutions.title: Growth and ownership capital
solutions.headline: Fund the growth. Shape the ownership.
solutions.intro: Put capital into the business, create shareholder liquidity or support a management transaction. Start with where the proceeds should go and what ownership should look like afterwards.
uses: Set out the expansion or acquisition plan and what new investment should enable.
Separate a shareholder sale from capital available to fund the company’s next plans.
Frame the buyout, acquisition or succession objective around management and shareholder alignment.
fit: An established business with a clear growth or ownership event
A credible management team and supporting commercial evidence
Shareholders willing to examine equity and governance trade-offs
solutions.notFit: A pre-revenue startup usually needs a stage-led venture conversation. A short cash-flow gap may be better explored through borrowing than a change in ownership.
solutions.mechanics: Distinguish newly issued equity, where proceeds go into the company, from shares sold by existing owners. A transaction can combine both. The business may receive a different amount from the headline deal value; ownership, governance, incentives and expectations about a later exit need to be considered together.
tradeoffs: Valuation and dilution
Understand the ownership being issued or transferred, how proceeds are used and the effect on existing shareholders.
Governance and control
Board roles, consent rights and other terms can affect decisions even in a minority investment.
Investor alignment
Sector, strategy, management expectations and future funding capacity need to fit the plan.
Process and exit
Diligence and shareholder agreement take time. Clarify the investor’s horizon and expectations about future liquidity.
prepare: The intended split between company investment and shareholder proceeds
Current ownership, management involvement and the decisions shareholders can support
Capital purpose, timetable, financial picture and existing advisers
faqs: Does equity always mean selling control?
No, but minority ownership does not mean an absence of governance rights. The proposed terms need specific review.
Is the highest valuation the best offer?
The full agreement matters: governance, conditions, incentives, investor fit and exit expectations can change the overall assessment.
Will my information be circulated to investors?
The scope of any introduction and information sharing should be agreed. A first conversation does not require sending a shareholder register or confidential pack.
solutions.fitHeading: A business ready for an ownership decision
solutions.preparationHeading: Outline the business and its owners
solutions.enquiryIntro: Explain the shareholder decision, where proceeds should go and the timetable.
solutions.fitIntro: An ownership event needs a credible business case and shareholders who can agree what should change. Investor fit and the full terms matter alongside the amount.
solutions.valueIntro: We help frame the use of proceeds, shareholder priorities and information needed for a relevant capital conversation. Separately agreed advisory work can support the investment proposition and ownership scenarios; any provider approach requires your go-ahead.

Discuss incentives, follow-on capital, shareholder alignment and future liquidity.

solutions.title: Venture funding
solutions.headline: Fund the milestone that moves you forward.
solutions.intro: Connect the next evidence point to the round, runway and investor profile it needs. Validation and commercial scaling require different funding cases.
uses: Define what still needs proving, the test or customer evidence sought and the cost to reach that point.
Align the milestone, investor proposition, use of proceeds and existing round status.
Show how capital supports delivery or growth, with unit economics, cash burn and later funding in view.
fit: A scalable company with an ambitious but evidenced plan
A defined milestone and a view of runway and future funding
Founders prepared to consider dilution and investor governance
solutions.notFit: Venture capital does not suit every startup. An ordinary working-capital requirement in an established company may be a business-funding conversation.
solutions.mechanics: Venture equity supports risk and growth in return for ownership. Investor stage, sector, geography and ability to lead or follow are important. Venture debt, where relevant, introduces repayment and may include covenants or warrants; it is not an automatic replacement for equity.
tradeoffs: Stage and investor mandate
Evidence appropriate to the round is more useful than a broad list of investors.
Ownership and rights
Compare dilution with preferences, governance, incentives and future rounds.
Runway and milestones
Allow for delays and future capital requirements. A milestone is not a guaranteed valuation increase.
Readiness and execution
Decks, forecasts, ownership and diligence need to tell a coherent story; a raise cannot be guaranteed.
prepare: Stage, customer or technical evidence and what remains unproven
The milestone, costed use of proceeds and runway to reach it
Current round status, existing investor discussions and future capital needs
faqs: Can a pre-revenue business raise capital?
Some investors consider early-stage risk, but the stage, evidence, opportunity and mandate must fit. Pre-revenue status alone does not establish suitability.
Can debt avoid dilution?
Some venture debt includes warrants and other commitments, alongside repayment. Compare the actual terms rather than assuming zero dilution.
Do I need to upload a pitch deck immediately?
No. A non-confidential summary can establish the initial context before agreeing whether and how more detailed material should be shared.

solutions.fitIntro: A venture case connects risk, evidence and a scalable opportunity. The round needs a defined milestone and realistic runway; stage, sector, geography and investor mandate must fit the actual company.
solutions.valueIntro: We help turn the stage, milestone and use of proceeds into a coherent capital requirement. Advisory support for forecasts, investor materials or ownership scenarios is scoped separately. A relevant investor approach depends on mandate and your agreement, not an assumed list of available investors.

solutions.title: Complex funding
solutions.headline: Start with the requirement and the real deadline.
solutions.intro: A maturing facility, a complex transaction or a change in trading: set out what must happen, by when and which decisions or consents stand in the way.
uses: Set out a facility maturity, lender change or refinancing constraint and what must happen next.
Explain the acquisition, carve-out or unusual structure and the stakeholders who need to agree.
Connect a credible operating plan with the immediate constraints and existing obligations.
fit: A clear account of the situation and its underlying business case
Current information and decision-makers able to engage
A realistic plan and willingness to involve appropriate specialists
solutions.notFit: Possible insolvency, imminent enforcement or questions about director duties can require urgent qualified professional advice. New borrowing is not a substitute for resolving an unviable plan.
solutions.mechanics: A complex capital requirement depends on viability, existing obligations, security and stakeholder support. The first task is to establish whether a funding route is realistic and what professional input or consents are needed.
tradeoffs: Viability before capital
Explain how the plan addresses the underlying issue rather than postponing it.
Stakeholder alignment
Existing lenders, shareholders and advisers may need to agree before a transaction can proceed.
Cost and priority
New capital can bring significant cost, security and conditions. These require candid assessment.
Timing and discretion
Share the real deadline and agree information handling. Do not assume immediate availability or absolute confidentiality.
prepare: What changed, what must happen next and any real deadline
A broad description of the plan, repayment or exit and existing obligations
The stakeholders, advisers and consents involved
faqs: Can funding solve every difficult situation?
No. Viability, professional advice and stakeholder decisions can matter before a capital route is considered.
Should I include detailed creditor information in an enquiry?
Start with a broad, non-sensitive summary. Agree a suitable secure process before sending detailed financial or legal material.
How quickly can the situation be assessed?
That depends on the information, complexity and actual specialist availability. A deadline is important context, not a guarantee of funding by that date.

solutions.structureHeading: Map the situation and the deadline
solutions.valueHeading: Organise the requirement before an approach
solutions.preparationHeading: Outline the situation without confidential detail

solutions.fitIntro: The first discussion separates the funding objective from the underlying issue. A viable plan, current information and the real deadline help establish whether a capital conversation is useful.
solutions.valueIntro: We first clarify what changed, the funding purpose, the available information and the critical decisions. Then we establish whether preparation, a provider discussion or specialist input is the appropriate next step. This is triage of the requirement, not a promise of immediate funding.

solutions.title: Life sciences funding
solutions.headline: Capital around your next scientific milestone.
solutions.intro: Connect the scientific or commercial milestone to its evidence, budget and runway. Discovery, development, commercial scale and laboratory investment need different capital conversations.
uses: Frame the next technical evidence point, remaining uncertainty and resources required.
Connect market evidence, delivery capacity and relevant approval dependencies to the capital plan.
Separate an operating laboratory’s equipment investment from science-led development risk.
fit: A clearly defined scientific or commercial milestone
An appropriate evidence base, team and rights to relevant IP
A realistic budget, runway and view of later capital needs
solutions.notFit: A pre-revenue development business and a profitable laboratory need different funding assessments. Scientific promise alone is not evidence of debt repayment capacity.
solutions.mechanics: Life sciences is a sector rather than one financing product. The stage, subsector and purpose determine whether an equity, operating-debt, equipment or other specialist conversation is relevant. Technical and regulatory assessment requires appropriate expertise.
tradeoffs: Milestone and contingency
Allow for development delays and costs beyond the immediate study or validation point.
Capital structure
Consider dilution, repayment and rights over IP in the context of development risk.
Specialist evidence
Provider understanding and relevant diligence matter; Frontier does not independently validate scientific outcomes.
Confidential information
Start with a non-confidential summary. Do not send patient data or unpublished research through an initial enquiry.
prepare: Subsector, current stage and the non-confidential milestone
Evidence already available, resources needed and the broad budget
Timing, runway, later capital needs and relevant specialist dependencies
faqs: Is this only for biotechnology companies?
Different life-sciences businesses have different requirements. Define the activity and stage so the relevant specialist scope can be established.
Can laboratory equipment be financed separately?
An operating business buying equipment may have a different capital case from a company funding uncertain development. The eligible costs and actual provider scope need to be checked.
Do I need to share confidential research?
Not at first contact. Begin with a non-confidential account of the requirement and agree any later information exchange.

solutions.commitmentsHeading: Development risk and later capital needs
solutions.enquiryHeading: Discuss the milestone and funding need

solutions.valueIntro: We help organise a non-confidential milestone outline and distinguish scientific development capital from operating or equipment investment. Scientific, technical and regulatory judgments require appropriately qualified specialists; we do not validate research outcomes.

solutions.title: Technology and equipment funding
solutions.headline: Put the next capability into productive use.
solutions.intro: Equipment, automation or a business technology investment: separate the purchase, installation and adoption costs, then match the funding conversation to when the capability becomes useful.
uses: Define the asset, supplier, delivery and commissioning requirements.
Separate licences, integration, training and ongoing service costs; eligibility depends on the actual facility.
Raising capital for a technology company?
Company fundraising belongs with stage, traction, ownership and runway—not an equipment purchase assessment.
fit: An operating business with a defined purchase or capability investment
A cost breakdown, implementation timetable and credible commercial case
A view of eligible costs, repayment and operating obligations
solutions.notFit: A technology label does not establish eligibility. Software, services and integration costs may be treated differently from equipment; an untested investment needs a credible business case.
solutions.mechanics: Asset and equipment finance is shaped by the asset, eligible expenditure, deposit, term and end-of-term obligations. Software, implementation and ongoing services may need different treatment. Match funding and repayment to delivery, installation and adoption rather than assuming the supplier quote is fully financeable.
tradeoffs: Eligible expenditure
Confirm what is actually financeable, including deposits, software, integration and service costs.
Delivery and repayment
Match commitments to installation, adoption and the timing of benefits; do not assume immediate savings.
Ownership and obligations
Clarify ownership or end-of-term options for assets and the conditions of any borrowing.
Company capital
A startup round introduces different ownership, investor and runway considerations from equipment finance.
prepare: The asset or capability, supplier quote and cost categories
Delivery, installation, training and expected productive-use dates
Commercial assumptions, existing obligations and repayment source
faqs: Can software and implementation costs be funded?
That depends on the product and provider. A quote should separate equipment, software, services and implementation so the scope can be assessed.
Will savings cover the repayments?
That is a business-case assumption to test, including delays and downside scenarios. Finance does not guarantee the expected return.
We are a technology startup. Which route should we use?
Start with the company’s stage and capital purpose. The venture or growth-capital journey may be more relevant than an equipment-finance discussion.

solutions.commitmentsHeading: Eligible costs and end of term obligations
solutions.valueHeading: Connect the investment to the operating plan

solutions.valueIntro: We help separate the expenditure, implementation dependencies and repayment case so the provider conversation reflects the actual purchase. Financial modelling or application preparation can be commissioned separately; expected capacity or savings remain assumptions to test.

solutions.title: Sustainability and impact funding
solutions.headline: Fund the investment behind the intended impact.
solutions.intro: Choose the commercial requirement first: improving an operating business or growing a business built around an environmental or social purpose. Then define the intended outcome and the evidence behind it.
solutions.cta: Discuss your investment or impact plan
uses: Cost an efficiency or cleaner-equipment investment alongside installation and delivery assumptions.
Connect the growth model, capital requirement and intended environmental or social outcome.
Identify the baseline, measurement method and what the investment could reasonably change.
fit: A viable commercial or investment case
A specific environmental or social objective
A proportionate way to explain and evidence the intended outcome
solutions.notFit: A worthwhile purpose does not automatically establish a repayment or investment case. A green asset is not necessarily an impact investment, grant or discounted loan.
solutions.mechanics: Funding a solar installation or cleaner equipment is different from an investor backing an impact-led company. The capital structure, eligible entity, commercial case and any reporting requirements must be considered separately.
tradeoffs: Commercial viability
Test the investment economics and delivery assumptions alongside the intended benefit.
Evidence and reporting
Clarify the baseline, measurement method and any provider-specific reporting obligations.
Actual product terms
Environmental purpose does not guarantee lower cost, a grant or preferential eligibility.
Delivery of outcomes
Be explicit about dependencies and uncertainty; avoid claims that the funding alone proves impact.
prepare: Operational investment or business-growth purpose and the costed plan
The baseline and intended environmental or social outcome
Delivery assumptions, measurement method and commercial evidence
faqs: Will sustainable finance be cheaper?
Not necessarily. Compare the actual product, terms, requirements and total cost rather than assuming a green label changes the price.
Is grant funding included?
Availability and support for grants must be confirmed separately. This page does not promise a grant or assume that a project qualifies.
Do we need formal impact reporting?
Requirements vary by route and provider. Measurement should be appropriate to the intended outcome and any actual funding conditions.

solutions.headline: Capital for the business behind the insurance.
solutions.intro: For brokers, MGAs, insurtechs and risk carriers: frame the capital purpose around the entity, commercial model and transaction. Business funding is distinct from insurance cover or underwriting capacity.
solutions.scopeNote: Business-capital requirements for brokers, MGAs, insurtechs and risk carriers. The relevant specialist support and provider fit are established for each engagement; this is not a policy, claims or underwriting-capacity service.
uses: Describe the broker, MGA, insurtech or risk-carrier transaction and the shareholder objective.
Explain what the business capital would fund and how the commercial model supports the case.
Identify the entity type, activity, jurisdiction and specialist dependencies before a provider approach.
fit: A clearly defined business-capital purpose
An identifiable entity, activity and jurisdiction
A willingness to establish specialist and regulatory dependencies
solutions.notFit: Insurance cover, claims support and underwriting capacity are separate services. Their availability must not be inferred from this capital page.
solutions.mechanics: A broker acquisition, an MGA growth plan and an insurer’s capital requirement involve different structures and specialists. The initial task is to define the requirement and establish whether it falls within a genuinely supported service.
tradeoffs: Entity and activity
Use precise language about what the business does and what capital is intended to achieve.
Specialist scope
Relevant expertise and actual provider appetite must be verified before an introduction is proposed.
Structural dependencies
Ownership, governance and relevant regulatory matters require appropriate review.
Capital versus cover
A business-capital conversation is not advice on or arrangement of an insurance policy.
prepare: Broker, MGA, insurtech or risk carrier; activity and jurisdiction
Capital purpose, transaction stage and ownership objective where relevant
Commercial evidence, broad timing and existing specialist advisers
faqs: Can I buy insurance cover here?
No. This page covers business-capital requirements, not insurance policies or claims services.
Is underwriting capacity the same as growth capital?
No. They are distinct requirements and may involve different specialist counterparties.
Is this service available for every insurance entity?
The retained scope includes brokers, MGAs, insurtechs and risk carriers. Relevant expertise, activity, jurisdiction and provider criteria still need to fit the individual requirement.

solutions.title: Digital Asset Business Funding
solutions.headline: Fund the operating business behind the digital assets.
solutions.intro: For blockchain and digital-asset businesses, begin with what the company does, where it operates and what the capital must achieve. Technology is context; the operating model is the funding case.
solutions.scopeNote: Operating-company capital for blockchain and digital-asset businesses. This is not a token sale, retail crypto investment, trading service or physical data-centre, telecoms or cloud-infrastructure offering.
uses: Explain the company’s commercial technology, users and revenue model. This is not funding for physical data centres or telecoms.
Connect customers and operating evidence to the people and systems needed for growth.
Describe the next commercial or delivery milestone, resources and operating dependencies.
fit: A transparent operating business and defined capital purpose
A clear description of the activity and jurisdiction
Commercial, ownership and financial information available for appropriate review
solutions.notFit: Retail token purchases, trading signals, promised returns and anonymous operations are outside this proposed business-capital journey. Provider appetite cannot be assumed from a sector label.
solutions.mechanics: Software and infrastructure companies, exchanges, custodians and token-related businesses are different activities. The capital route and specialist scope depend on the actual operating model, jurisdiction, evidence and counterparties willing to assess it.
tradeoffs: Activity and jurisdiction
Establish what the business actually does and where; do not treat the sector as one eligibility category.
Commercial evidence
Technology enthusiasm is not a substitute for customers, a capital plan and appropriate operating evidence.
Governance and risk
Operational, security, market and legal dependencies need appropriate specialist assessment.
Status and claims
Registration or a provider relationship should never be described as blanket regulatory approval or protection.
prepare: Plain-language operating activity and company jurisdiction
Customers, revenues or other commercial evidence appropriate to the stage
Use of funds, next business milestone and broad timing
faqs: Can I buy crypto or invest in tokens here?
No. This page is a business-capital concept and does not offer tokens, investments or return promises.
Will every funding provider consider a blockchain business?
No. Appetite depends on the actual activity, jurisdiction, business evidence and provider mandate.
Should I connect a wallet or upload identity documents?
No. An initial enquiry should not require wallet connections, private keys, account access or identity documents.
